javascript.childprocess.exec.a0.summary: Executes a command through the host shell; treat user-controlled input as a command-injection boundary.
javascript.childprocess.exec.a0.safe_pattern: Prefer an argument-array API with a fixed executable and explicit allow-list.

python.pickle.load.a0.summary: Deserializes a pickle stream and can execute code during object reconstruction.
python.pickle.load.a0.safe_pattern: Use a data-only format such as JSON when the payload is not fully trusted.

c.std.system.a0.summary: Passes a string to the system command processor; shell metacharacters make the boundary especially sensitive.
c.std.system.a0.safe_pattern: Avoid shell parsing; use a direct process API and fixed arguments.

javascript.shell-quote.quote.a0-ret.summary: Quotes a shell argument for a specific shell grammar. This is a sanitizer, not proof that the overall command is safe.
javascript.shell-quote.quote.a0-ret.safe_pattern: Prefer removing the shell boundary entirely; quote only as a constrained compatibility measure.

javascript.std.eval.a0.summary: Evaluates a string as JavaScript in the current execution context; untrusted text becomes executable code.
javascript.std.eval.a0.safe_pattern: Keep code and data separate. Use a parser or a constrained expression language when evaluation is unavoidable.

typescript.std.eval.a0.summary: Evaluates a string as JavaScript in the current execution context; untrusted text becomes executable code.
typescript.std.eval.a0.safe_pattern: Keep code and data separate. Use a parser or a constrained expression language when evaluation is unavoidable.

python.builtins.eval.a0.summary: Evaluates a Python expression with ambient globals and locals, making input-to-code transitions difficult to constrain.
python.builtins.eval.a0.safe_pattern: Parse structured data or expose a small allow-listed operation set instead of evaluating source text.

python.os.system.a0.summary: Hands a command string to the operating system shell, preserving shell expansion and metacharacter behavior.
python.os.system.a0.safe_pattern: Use subprocess with an argument list and shell disabled; validate each argument for its intended domain.

python.subprocess.run.a0.summary: Starts a process from caller-controlled arguments; the security boundary depends on argument construction and shell mode.
python.subprocess.run.a0.safe_pattern: Pass a sequence of fixed executable and arguments, keep shell=False, and constrain executable selection.

python.yaml.load.a0.summary: Loads YAML with a loader whose behavior depends on the selected constructor set; unsafe constructors can instantiate objects.
python.yaml.load.a0.safe_pattern: Use SafeLoader or a data-only YAML parser when documents are not fully trusted.

python.yaml.unsafeload.a0.summary: Explicitly enables YAML constructors that can create Python objects from input, making the deserializer a code-execution boundary.
python.yaml.unsafeload.a0.safe_pattern: Do not use this loader for attacker-controlled documents; prefer safe_load and a schema.

c.std.memcpy.a0.summary: Copies a caller-supplied byte count into a destination without inherent bounds checking.
c.std.memcpy.a0.safe_pattern: Carry destination capacity alongside the buffer and use a bounded operation with a checked length.
